text: A protocol specification defines only the format of the messages exchanged. What is missing?
choices: Nothing — format is what a protocol is
Semantics and timing: what the fields mean and in what sequence messages may be sent
explanation: A protocol is an agreement on syntax (format), semantics (meaning and obligations), and timing (the permitted sequence, i.e. the state machine). A specification with only the first is a data structure. Most of TCP's complexity lives in the third clause, not the first.
